what: 14. Connectivity and Genomic Prediction: Simulation Illustration
title: OptiSparseMET: A Unified Framework for Sparse Multi-Environment Trial Design
text: Cross-environment connectivity matters genotype performance varies across environments – , genotype--environment interaction (G x E). therefore evaluate designs genuine G x E model genotype--environment effects covariance Sigma_E %x% G (genetic correlation structure across environments, single shared breeding value). met_information() returns coupled across-TPE prediction-error variance (PEV) reliability (CDmean); simulate_met() returns realized selection accuracy genetic gain designs achieve. fully balanced design positive control (highest accuracy, lowest PEV). Among sparse options, environment-pair-balanced optimize_allocation_gxe()-refined allocations recover accuracy plain random sparse allocation, distribute cross-environment connectivity evenly – exactly property coupled information matrix rewards. size advantage grows spread genetic correlations Sigma_E (broad TPE) shrinks TPE narrows.
code: set.seed(1) n_geno <- 120 n_env  <- 4 lines  <- paste0("L", seq_len(n_geno)) envs   <- paste0("E", seq_len(n_env))  # Genomic relationship matrix M  <- matrix(rnorm(n_geno^2), n_geno) G0 <- tcrossprod(M) / n_geno diag(G0) <- diag(G0) + 0.5 dimnames(G0) <- list(lines, lines)  # Broad TPE: environments with a mix of positive and negative genetic # correlations (this is what makes connectivity matter). Sigma_E <- matrix(c( 1.0,  0.6,  0.2, -0.1,                      0.6,  1.0,  0.3,  0.0,                      0.2,  0.3,  1.0,  0.5,                     -0.1,  0.0,  0.5,  1.0), 4, 4)  # Fully balanced positive control: every line in every environment. alloc_full <- matrix(1L, n_geno, n_env, dimnames = list(lines, envs))  # Random sparse allocation, each line in ~2 of 4 environments. alloc_sparse <- allocate_sparse_met(   treatments                     = lines,   environments                   = envs,   allocation_method              = "random_balanced",   n_test_entries_per_environment = 60,   target_replications            = 2,   allow_approximate              = TRUE,   seed                           = 1 )$allocation_matrix  # Equireplicate allocation with environment-pair connectivity balancing # (near-balanced / regular-graph design). alloc_eqr <- allocate_sparse_met(   treatments                     = lines,   environments                   = envs,   allocation_method              = "equireplicate",   n_test_entries_per_environment = 60,   target_replications            = 2,   balance                        = "env_pair",   seed                           = 1 )$allocation_matrix  # Refine the equireplicate allocation directly against the coupled G x E # objective (minimise across-TPE PEV). alloc_opt <- optimize_allocation_gxe(   alloc_eqr, G = G0, Sigma_E = Sigma_E, iter = 100, seed = 1 )$allocation_matrix  # Design-based coupled PEV / CDmean (lower PEV, higher CDmean is better). sapply(list(full = alloc_full, sparse = alloc_sparse,             equireplicate = alloc_eqr, optimised = alloc_opt),        function(A) met_information(A, G = G0, Sigma_E = Sigma_E)$mean_PEV)  # Realized selection accuracy and genetic gain across the TPE. sapply(list(full = alloc_full, sparse = alloc_sparse,             equireplicate = alloc_eqr, optimised = alloc_opt),        function(A) simulate_met(A, G = G0, Sigma_E = Sigma_E,                                 n_sim = 50, seed = 1)$accuracy_mean)

OptiSparseMET provides following: allocation level: two complementary strategies (M3 flexible approximate balance, M4 design-based uniformity), diagnostic tools verifying feasibility allocation attempted, genetic structure awareness family, GRM, pedigree-based grouping. field design level: two design engines complementary strengths (met_prep_famoptg() block-based repeated-check layouts, met_alpha_rc_stream() fixed-grid row-column designs), efficiency evaluation , D, CDmean criteria, criterion-driven optimisation via three methods (RS, SA, GA). Linking levels: seed feasibility verification ensures designs operationally deployable; common treatment support ensures design-based connectivity; pipeline functions (plan_sparse_met_design(), combine_met_fieldbooks()) ensure outputs levels consistent assembled unified MET field book. result workflow produces designs statistically grounded operationally deployable — rather optimizing one expense .

what: Answering the five decision points — a corrected, package-native design
title: Answering the five decision points — a corrected, package-native design
text: Prepared F. Akohoue — 2026-07-21. Companion IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md CRITIQUE_Colmant2026_and_OptiSparseMET.md. Goal: make OptiSparseMET give genuine, criterion-driven, validated answer decision point Colmant et al. (2026), Figure 1 — correcting weaknesses objective functions interpretation. Every method presented modified version paper’s idea, package name explicit statement changed . Nothing claims reproduce paper intact. five decision points: 1. & many locations best represent TPE? 2. & many individuals best represent TPG? 3. allocate representative set entries across environments? 4. many replicates per entry planted? 5. spread entries plots within environment?

what: Two systemic corrections that make all five answers sound
title: Answering the five decision points — a corrected, package-native design
text: fix interpretation errors paper otherwise contaminate every decision, apply package-wide. S1 — force single “TPE-average” breeding-value target. paper defines accuracy average true BV across environments, estimated main-effect-model, even though data simulated strong G×E. structurally favors broad adaptation makes allocation look unimportant. evaluation harness (simulate_met(), met_information()) support three explicit targets — across-TPE mean, environment-specific, mega-environment/cluster BVs — fit G×E-aware model (factor-analytic / unstructured Sigma_E), main-effect-. Every “better” answer reported per target specific adaptation silently penalized. S2 — Replace unbounded “spread” proxies quantity determines accuracy. paper’s workhorse -q'Dq (underspecified connectedness Eqs 2–3) maximize mutual dissimilarity, representativeness prediction reliability. Wherever paper uses -q'Dq, () keep clearly labeled spread baseline, (b) add CDmean/PEV-based objective computed real information matrix recommended default. single important scientific upgrade reused across decisions 1, 2, 3.

what: Decision 1 — Which & how many locations best represent the TPE?
title: Answering the five decision points — a corrected, package-native design
text: Paper’s approach. Select n environments modified optimal-contribution function f(q) = -q'Dq (D = environment relationship), compared k-means, hierarchical clustering, random; “many” chosen plot-budget grid. Weaknesses (critique). -q'Dq maximizes spread, can pick mutually uncorrelated outlier environments miss TPE’s typical conditions; method comparison uncontrolled (different inputs, unequal compute); E assumed known; “many” never tied criterion. modified answer — select_environments() (modified optimal-contribution, representativeness-corrected). - Objective (default): representativeness-CDmean. Choose environment subset maximizes reliability predicting unselected remainder TPE — environment-level analogue Rincent-style training-set optimization. directly encodes “represents TPE,” unlike -q'Dq. - Objective (baseline): -q'Dq (spread) + optional mean-representativeness term w1·coverage − w2·q'Dq, documented diversity-maximizing. - Baselines retained: k-means, hclust, random — honest benchmarking identical inputs compute budget (fixing paper’s uncontrolled comparison). - “many”: criterion, budget. Return representativeness (predicted-TPE-accuracy) curve vs n, elbow/marginal-gain rule target-reliability stopping option. - E construction — build_environment_relationship(): historical MET genetic correlations enviromic covariates (weather/soil/remote sensing), trait-specificity caveat documented (enviromic E general, trait-specific, relationship). Naming: “Modified optimal-contribution environment selection (Colmant et al. 2026, decision 1), representativeness-corrected.” Validation: D planted redundant cluster, corrected objective avoids picking two near-identical environments random ; “many” curve monotone predicted-TPE accuracy broad-TPE simulation.

what: Decision 2 — Which & how many individuals best represent the TPG?
title: Answering the five decision points — a corrected, package-native design
text: Paper’s approach. Framed sparsity dimension (ia × ipf × noe grid); individuals mostly sampled random, -q'Dq available selection. Weaknesses. Random sampling weak answer “individuals represent”; representativeness objective TPG undeveloped; “many” simulation grid. modified answer — select_individuals() (CDmean training-set optimization) + sparsity_grid(). - : CDmean (Rincent et al. 2012) GRM. Select subset TPG maximizes CDmean predicting rest TPG — established, correct tool “representative/informative individuals.” principled upgrade random raw -q'Dq. - Diversity alternative: -q'Dq(G) exposed founder-contribution/spread baseline spread-vs-representativeness caveat. - many: sparsity_grid() explores ia × ipf × noe total-plot budget returns accuracy/Δg S1 harness cell, program locates sweet spot rather reading paper-specific number. Naming: “CDmean-based TPG representative-set selection (modified Colmant decision 2; objective Rincent et al. 2012).” Validation: selected set yields higher predicted accuracy held-TPG random equal size; grid respects plot budget.

what: Decision 3 — How to allocate a representative set of entries across environments?
title: Answering the five decision points — a corrected, package-native design
text: Paper’s approach. -q'Dq D = G ⊗ E optimized GA (evola); plus connectedness objective functions (Eqs 2–3). Weaknesses. Eqs 2–3 underspecified/non-reproducible (“details request”); -q'Dq(G⊗E) spread proxy; biased target + main-effect estimation made allocation look nearly irrelevant. Capacity, equal replication, common treatments, seed limits jointly handled. modified answer — allocate_sparse_met(objective = "optcontrib_GxE"), optimizing across-TPE CDmean. - Objective (default): across-TPE CDmean/PEV met_information() — MET-level information matrix combining allocation incidence Z G ⊗ Sigma_E. optimize quantity actually governs prediction accuracy, replacing underspecified Eqs 2–3 well-defined, reproducible criterion. - Structural constraints/objectives: near-balanced equireplicate concurrence environment-pair connectivity balance (allocation phase), connectedness property paper gestured never balanced. - Baseline: -q'Dq(G⊗E) spread objective retained labeled. - Constraints honored jointly: per-environment capacity, common treatments, seed availability (assign_replication_by_seed()), making allocation deployable — something paper omits. - Fair evaluation (S1): assessed G×E model per target, “allocation matter?” question answered without paper’s model-misspecification. Naming: “Modified connectedness allocation (Colmant decision 3): CDmean-based G×E objective replacing Eqs 2–3.” Validation: objective improves across-TPE PEV vs random allocation broad-TPE case; narrow TPE gain shrinks (matching paper’s qualitative finding, now sound basis).

what: Decision 4 — How many replicates per entry should be planted?
title: Answering the five decision points — a corrected, package-native design
text: Paper’s approach. Grid field size (100–900 plots) × replication (1.0–2.0); conclusion: replication matters little GRM used; ~400 plots needed high spatial noise. Weaknesses. Field size confounded number unique entries; conclusions specific extreme spatial-noise setting; seed constraint; replication reported scalar average. modified answer — recommend_replication() (resource- noise-aware), built assign_replication_by_seed(). - Criterion-driven, static grid. Given program’s spatial- variance level, GRM, seed availability, sweep replication level p-rep fraction return accuracy/Δg-per-unit-cost curve; recommend level diminishing-returns point. - De-confound size vs replication (fixing paper). Hold number unique entries fixed varying replication, separately vary field size, two effects reported independently. - Seed realism. Recommendations feasible seed limits — package’s existing strength, now wired replication decision. Naming: “Resource-aware replication optimization (modified Colmant decision 4; confounding field size replication corrected; seed constraints added).” Validation: low-noise scenario recommended replication differs high-noise scenario (showing noise-dependence single-setting paper ); recommendations never exceed seed availability.

what: Decision 5 — How to spread entries in plots within an environment?
title: Answering the five decision points — a corrected, package-native design
text: Paper’s approach. Compare random, -optimality (odw), genetic--spatial connectedness design (GbySpat, Eqs 2–3); report accuracy compute time. Weaknesses. GbySpat (Eqs 2–3) reproducible; -optimality via odw expensive. decision package already covers best — P0 correctness bugs (AR1 indexing, CDmean scaling) yet trustworthy. modified answer — existing within-environment engine, corrected extended. - Constructors: met_prep_famoptg() (augmented / p-rep / RCBD) met_alpha_rc_stream() (alpha row-column) — already present. - Evaluation (P0 fixes): / D / corrected CDmean IID / AR1 / AR1×AR1 residuals — correct, reproducible replacement paper’s -optimality vs GbySpat comparison. - defined GbySpat objective (modified, reproducible): minimize spatially-weighted genomic-relationship clustering penalty — .e. spread genetically similar lines apart field — , equivalently, directly maximize CDmean AR1×AR1 residual. gives paper’s “genetic--spatial” idea explicit, documented formula instead “details request.” - Search: RS / SA / GA (met_optimize_*), reporting compute time like paper accuracy-vs-cost trade-transparent. Naming: “Genetic--spatial within-field optimization (modified Colmant decision 5): explicit spatially-weighted relationship objective / AR1×AR1 CDmean.” Validation: closed-form /D oracles (P2.1) AR1 test (P0.1) guarantee criteria correct; optimized designs beat random family-clustered adverse control realized accuracy (matching paper’s direction, now bug-free).

text: plan_sparse_met_design() orchestrate corrected decisions end end, step feeding next reporting criterion value: step optimizes defined, validated criterion (whole chain can scored simulate_met() realized accuracy/Δg G×E model), package answers paper’s questions genuinely — , paper’s objective interpretation weak, answers better, honest “modified Colmant et al. (2026)” label.

title: OptiSparseMET — Sparse Multi-Environment Trial Design
text: OptiSparseMET R framework constructing sparse multi-environment trials (METs) jointly addresses treatment allocation across environments field design within environments – shared statistical, genetic, logistical constraints. package targets structural challenge common modern breeding programs: number candidate lines routinely exceeds single environment can accommodate, environments heterogeneous rather interchangeable, seed availability imposes limits purely theoretical designs ignore. Standard MET tools typically address one problems time. OptiSparseMET integrates within single workflow.

title: OptiSparseMET — Sparse Multi-Environment Trial Design
text: Sparse MET design two-level problem treated . Level 1 — Across-environment allocation determines treatments appear environments, many times treatment replicated across trial, whether resulting incidence structure preserves sufficient genetic connectivity valid cross-environment inference. Level 2 — Within-environment design determines blocking structure, spatial layout, replication within environment, local control field heterogeneity. two levels merely sequential steps — statistically coupled, optimizing independently produces inferior designs. linkage operates four mechanisms. 1. incidence matrix couples levels inside information matrix. linear mixed model: \(y = X\beta + Zg + e\), precision genetic value estimates governed coefficient matrix: \(C = Z^\top V^{-1} Z - Z^\top V^{-1} X(X^\top V^{-1} X)^{-1} X^\top V^{-1} Z\), \(V = ZKZ^\top \sigma_g^2 + R\sigma_e^2\). allocation decision determines sparsity pattern \(Z\) (lines appear ); within-environment blocking structure determines \(R\) (residual covariance). enter \(V\) therefore \(C^{-1}\). Neither can optimized isolation interact inside inversion \(V\). 2. Allocation fixes within-environment designs feasible. allocation assigns \(k_e\) lines environment \(e\), within-environment design must arrange exactly \(k_e\) treatments across available \(n_{\text{rows}} \times n_{\text{cols}}\) field. \(k_e\) incompatible blocking structure — example, multiple target block size, exceeding field capacity — design infeasible regardless statistically ideal allocation . Allocation field geometry must co-designed. 3. Block efficiency propagates cross-environment inference. precision genetic value estimate line \(j\) environment \(e\) proportional \(e_j \, r_j^{(e)}\), \(r_j^{(e)}\) number plots \(e_j \(0, 1]\) efficiency factor within-environment design relative completely randomized layout. poor block design reduces \(e_j\), inflating variance BLUP. inflated variances propagate cross-environment covariance estimates, degrading G×E inference genetic correlation estimation even allocation incidence structure perfectly balanced. 4. CDmean — genomic prediction criterion — depends levels. CDmean criterion, \(\text{CDmean} = 1 - \overline{\text{PEV}} / \sigma_g^2\), PEV depends \(Z\) (allocation) \(R^{-1}\) (blocking), maximized fixing either level independently. Spreading genetically diverse lines across environments improves genomic connectivity captured \(Z^\top R^{-1} Z\); efficient blocking sharpens \(R^{-1}\). contributions necessary. OptiSparseMET formalizes link two levels: allocation output specifies exactly lines enter environment, within-environment design engine receives precisely set, ensuring incidence structure blocking structure optimized consistently within statistical framework. coupling made concrete met_information(), assembles across-environment (MET-level) information matrix allocation incidence (Level 1) within-environment efficiency factor (Level 2) G × E model (Sigma_E ⊗ G), returns across-TPE mean PEV CDmean. simulate_met() reports realized selection accuracy genetic gain designs achieve, optimize_allocation_gxe() optimizes allocation directly coupled objective.

title: OptiSparseMET — Sparse Multi-Environment Trial Design
text: Two strategies available, inspired M3 M4 Montesinos-Lopez et al. (2023): Note terminology. "equireplicate" accurate name M4-type constructor (paper’s "M4" label also accepted alias). strict balanced incomplete block design (BIBD): strict BIBD requires constant pairwise concurrence λ, — integrality λ = r(k−1)/(J−1) Fisher’s inequality ≥ J — generally exist treatments greatly outnumber environments (usual sparse-testing case). constructor therefore guarantees equal replication equal environment size, balance targets achievable near-balanced concurrence. what: Equireplicate – equal replication and equal environment sizes
title: OptiSparseMET — Sparse Multi-Environment Trial Design
text: equireplicate method (M4-type; Montesinos-Lopez et al. 2023) enforces two structural guarantees: Equal replication — every non-common treatment appears exactly \(r\) environments. Equal environment sizes — every environment receives exactly k* sparse treatments, enforcing resource identity J* × r = × k* exactly, J* = J − C k* = k − C (C = number common treatments). guarantees distinguish M4 M3 paper. plant breeding programs thousands lines tested across environments, equal replication means every candidate evaluated number times – fundamental fairness precision requirement. allow_approximate = FALSE (default) enforces conditions strictly. slot identity J* × r = × k* hold chosen dimensions, function stops clear error allocation attempted. Use check_balanced_incomplete_feasibility() verify slot identity first, adjust k r identity holds. Construction uses greedy load-balanced constructor guarantees equal replication. allow_approximate = TRUE relaxes slot identity allows minor replication imbalances. fallback exploratory use, primary mode.

Identity: 110*2 = 4*55 = 220. Holds. check_balanced_incomplete_feasibility(   n_treatments_total             = 120,   n_environments                 = 4,   n_test_entries_per_environment = 65,   target_replications            = 2,   n_common_treatments            = 10 ) # feasible = TRUE: 110*2 = 4*55 = 220 (difference = 0)  # Step 1a: M3-inspired random balanced allocation alloc_m3 <- allocate_sparse_met(   treatments                     = treatments,   environments                   = envs,   allocation_method              = "random_balanced",   n_test_entries_per_environment = 41,   target_replications            = 1,   common_treatments              = common,   seed                           = 123 )  alloc_m3$summary$min_sparse_replication  # every treatment in >= 1 environment alloc_m3$summary$mean_sparse_replication  # Step 1b: M4 BIBD allocation -- slot identity must hold exactly. # J*=110, I=4, r=2: k* = 110*2/4 = 55, k = 55+10 = 65. # Slot identity: 110*2 = 4*55 = 220. text: met_prep_famoptg() OptiSparseMET version prep_famoptg() OptiDesign package. met_ prefix avoids namespace conflicts packages loaded simultaneously. arguments, return values, internal logic identical prep_famoptg() OptiDesign. met_prep_famoptg() builds repeated-check block design plant breeding agronomic experiments. Check treatments included every block, non-check treatments allocated according user-specified replication levels. Depending treatment structure supplied, function generates three design classes: Augmented repeated-check design: checks repeated every block, test entries unreplicated (p_rep_treatments = NULL). Partially replicated (p-rep) repeated-check design: mixture replicated unreplicated non-check entries. RCBD-type repeated-check design: non-check entries given replication across blocks. Design evaluation separated construction. function returns field book, layout matrix, seed . compute , D, CDmean optimality criteria call met_evaluate_famoptg_efficiency() returned field_book. search optimised design across many randomisations call met_optimize_famoptg().

text: Let: \(c\) = number check treatments \(b\) = n_blocks \(v_p\) = number p-rep treatments replication counts \(r_1, r_2, \ldots, r_{v_p}\) \(v_u\) = number unreplicated treatments Total plots required: $$\text{total} = b \times c + \sum_{=1}^{v_p} r_i + v_u$$ Allocation rules enforced construction: Checks Appear every block. check contributes \(b\) plots total. title: Compute the minimum per-environment capacity for full treatment coverage — min_k_for_full_coverage
text: Let \(J\) total number treatments, \(C\) number common treatments assigned every environment, \(\) number environments. number sparse (non-common) treatments : $$J^* = J - C$$ Common treatments consume \(C\) slots every environment sparse allocation begins. number sparse-allocatable slots per environment : $$k_e^* = k_e - C$$ every sparse treatment appear least one environment, total number sparse slots across environments must satisfy: $$\sum_{e=1}^{} k_e^* \geq J^*$$ equal per-environment capacity, minimum number sparse slots per environment : $$k^*_{\min} = \left\lceil J^* / \right\rceil$$ corresponding minimum total entries per environment : $$k_{\min} = k^*_{\min} + C$$ function returns quantities. value min_total_entries_per_environment passed n_test_entries_per_environment guarantee full coverage minimum capacity.

Adjusting dimensions.  dim(out_prep$layout_matrix)   # 6 x 8 #> [1] 6 7 head(out_prep$field_book) #>        Treatment Family Gcluster Block Plot Row Column #> plot_1      L008    F06     <NA>     1    1   1      1 #> plot_2      L012    F14     <NA>     1    2   1      2 #> plot_3      CHK2  CHECK     <NA>     1    3   1      3 #> plot_4      L015    F10     <NA>     1    4   1      4 #> plot_5      L002    F15     <NA>     1    5   1      5 #> plot_6      L007    F02     <NA>     1    6   1      6 out_prep$seed_used #> [1] 123  if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ## Example 2: augmented repeated-check design — no replicated entries, ## all 24 test entries unreplicated. out_aug <- prep_famoptg(   check_treatments         = c("CHK1", "CHK2"),   check_families           = c("CHECK", "CHECK"),   p_rep_treatments         = character(0),   p_rep_reps               = integer(0),   p_rep_families           = character(0),   unreplicated_treatments  = env_trt,   unreplicated_families    = env_fam,   n_blocks                 = 4,   n_rows                   = 5,   n_cols                   = 6,   order                    = "row",   serpentine               = FALSE,   seed                     = 123,   cluster_source           = "Family",   eval_efficiency          = FALSE,   use_dispersion           = FALSE )  dim(out_aug$layout_matrix) head(out_aug$field_book)  ## Example 3: RCBD-type repeated-check design — all 24 entries replicated ## 4 times (once per block). Fixed offsetting extraction index ncol(X); verified independent dense MME solve (single-cell example: corrected mean_PEV = 0.55, previously 0.6625). AR1 / AR1×AR1 residual precision: fixed transposed Kronecker index swapped row/column autocorrelation axes scrambled spatial adjacency non-square fields. Residual-precision construction now centralised tested helper .build_residual_precision() verified hand-built AR1×AR1 precision (test-ar1-precision.R). Affects every AR1-based /D/CDmean value met_evaluate_alpha_efficiency() met_evaluate_famoptg_efficiency(). CDmean scaling: per-line reliability now divides sigma_g2 * K_ii (diagonal relationship matrix) instead sigma_g2 alone, correcting value VanRaden GRMs inbred/pedigree material diag(K) != 1. D-criterion: .safe_logdet_psd_dense() now uses relative eigenvalue tolerance exact expected rank, making pseudo-determinant scale-robust. Rank-deficiency guard: singular fixed-effects design (e.g. intercept plus full dummy set check rows) now repaired instead erroring.

title: OptiSparseMET 0.2.0 (development)
text: "AR1xAR1_nugget" adds independent measurement-error (nugget) component. Pure AR1xAR1 often fits field data poorly, usually realistic applied model. "exponential", "gaussian", "matern" give isotropic correlation function Euclidean plot distance, irregular non-rectangular layouts. build covariance observed plots invert (marginal form), also handle designs empty cells correctly. New spatial_random = "pspline" fits SpATS-style two-dimensional penalised-spline surface random effect (Rodriguez-Alvarez et al. 2018) rather residual covariance. tensor B-spline penalty improper (null space constant plus linear trends), block supplied mixed-model reparameterisation: positive-eigenvalue space kept, giving proper random effect whose surface shrinks away smoothing parameters grow. Available evaluators optimisers. New compare_spatial_models() scores one design several spatial models side side – spatial analogue sensitivity_varcomp(). design wins every model safe choice; one wins single model warning.

title: OptiSparseMET 0.2.0 (development)
text: met_evaluate_alpha_efficiency() / met_evaluate_famoptg_efficiency() now also return A_efficiency_rel, classical relative -efficiency (0, 1] (vs orthogonal CRD plots). existing A_efficiency / $fields documented inverse criterion, relative efficiency. New sensitivity_varcomp(): sweep residual/genetic variance ratio report across-TPE PEV CDmean respond, design choice can judged robustness variance misspecification. genuine contrast-based CDmean Rincent et al. (2012) available via select_individuals(); evaluators’ per-line quantity now correctly labeled reliability (see P0 CDmean fix) rather mislabeled Rincent CDmean. New met_information(): across-environment (MET-level) coupled information matrix. combines allocation incidence (Level 1) within-environment efficiency factor (Level 2) G x E model (Sigma_E ⊗ G) returns across-TPE mean PEV CDmean. backs “coupled two-level” claim code; fixed-effect absorption verified match full mixed-model-equations solve. New simulate_met(): simulates MET genuine across-environment genetic correlation structure, predicts GBLUP, reports realized selection accuracy genetic gain – linking /D/CDmean design proxies outcome meant improve (replaces previous -G×E vignette demonstration).

title: OptiSparseMET 0.2.0 (development)
text: New select_environments() (decision 1): choose representative subset environments TPE. Default "representative" maximises TPE coverage (k-medoid), correcting spread--q'Dq criterion (available "optcontrib"); "kmeans", "hclust", "random" baselines included. New select_individuals() (decision 2): choose representative training subset TPG maximising CDmean (Rincent et al. 2012) via exchange algorithm. New optimize_allocation_gxe() (decision 3): refine equireplicate allocation minimise across-TPE PEV coupled G x E information matrix – reproducible, CDmean-based replacement paper’s unbounded -q'Dq / connectedness objectives, preserving replication environment-size margins. New recommend_replication() (decision 4): sweep replication levels allocation, report realized accuracy / gain / PEV via simulate_met(), honour seed budget, recommend diminishing-returns level – de-confounding replication number unique entries.

title: OptiSparseMET 0.2.0 (development)
text: met_prep_famoptg() now emits field-dimension auto-correction informational message verbose (matching documented “silently adjusts” behaviour) instead warning(). plan_sparse_met_design() accepts allocation_method = "equireplicate" ("M4" alias).

title: OptiSparseMET 0.2.0 (development)
text: Renamed allocation_method = "balanced_incomplete" "equireplicate" (old name misnomer removed, deprecated; "M4" remains alias): constructor guarantees equal replication equal environment size, strict BIBD. bundled example data argument list likewise renamed sparse_example_args_equireplicate. New balance argument ("env_pair", "line_pair", "") drives design toward near-balanced (regular-graph) structure preserving replication environment-size margins; returns balance_report. check_equireplicate_feasibility() (retained check_balanced_incomplete_feasibility()) now report strict-BIBD existence conditions: bibd_lambda, bibd_lambda_integer, fisher_ok, strict_bibd_possible. New construct_exact_bibd() builds true BIBD via crossdes one provably exists (small-J regime).

title: OptiSparseMET 0.1.0
text: OptiSparseMET introduces unified framework sparse multi-environment trial (MET) design, jointly addressing treatment allocation across environments within-environment field design shared statistical, genetic, logistical constraints. package links allocation structure, genetic connectivity, seed availability, spatial design assumptions single reproducible workflow compatible mixed-model inference.

title: OptiSparseMET 0.1.0
text: Added allocate_sparse_met() constructing treatment--environment incidence matrices using sparse testing principles. Supports "random_balanced" (M3) flexible approximate balance coverage-first guarantees. Supports "balanced_incomplete" (M4) BIBD-inspired uniform replication structure enforced equal replication equal environment sizes across trial. Accepts "M3" "M4" convenient aliases. Supports unequal environment capacities random_balanced. Supports common treatments ensure design-based connectivity across environments. Returns $allocation_matrix (binary treatment--environment incidence matrix) pairwise co-occurrence can computed post-hoc $allocation_matrix %*% t($allocation_matrix). Added check_balanced_incomplete_feasibility() verify slot identity (J* × r = × k*) attempting balanced incomplete allocation, confirming equal replication achievable chosen dimensions. Added derive_allocation_groups() construct grouping structures : family membership labels genomic relationship matrix (GRM) pedigree relationship matrix (matrix) Group-guided allocation improves genetic connectedness stability cross-environment inference.

title: OptiSparseMET 0.1.0
text: Added suggest_safe_k() propose safe uniform value n_test_entries_per_environment given treatment count, environment count, common treatments, user-defined buffer. Added min_k_for_full_coverage() compute minimum per-environment capacity required every non-common treatment assigned least . Added warn_if_k_too_small() provide non-fatal diagnostic warning chosen capacity insufficient full treatment coverage. helpers prevent common failure mode: passing capacity small assign treatments allocate_sparse_met() called.

title: OptiSparseMET 0.1.0
text: Supports "augmented", "p_rep", "rcbd_type" replication modes. Supports shortage_action values "error", "downgrade", "exclude" handling treatments insufficient seed. Returns role-partitioned list (p_rep_treatments, unreplicated_treatments, excluded_treatments) suitable direct input met_prep_famoptg().

title: OptiSparseMET 0.1.0
text: Added met_prep_famoptg() constructing augmented, partially replicated (p-rep), RCBD-type repeated-check block designs. Key structural guarantees: Check treatments appear every block. Replicated (p-rep) treatments appear per block. Unreplicated treatments appear exactly across field. Optional genetic dispersion optimisation using GRM matrix. Optional within-environment efficiency evaluation (, D, CDmean). Added met_evaluate_famoptg_efficiency() evaluating statistical efficiency met_prep_famoptg() designs : Fixed random treatment effects. IID, AR1, AR1×AR1 residual covariance structures. -optimality, D-efficiency, CDmean, mean PEV criteria. Requires sigma_b2 (block variance) varcomp. Added met_optimize_famoptg() criterion-driven optimisation met_prep_famoptg() designs via Random Restart.

title: OptiSparseMET 0.1.0
text: Added met_alpha_rc_stream() generating alpha row-column stream designs suitable large structured fields. Key features: Repeated checks every incomplete block. Configurable block sizes via min_block_size / max_block_size fixed n_blocks_per_rep. Row-major, column-major, serpentine traversal orders. Optional genetic grouping family, GRM, matrix. Optional within-environment efficiency evaluation. Added met_evaluate_alpha_efficiency() evaluating statistical efficiency met_alpha_rc_stream() designs criteria met_evaluate_famoptg_efficiency(). Requires sigma_rep2 (replicate variance) sigma_ib2 (incomplete block within replicate variance) varcomp, distinguishing block-based evaluator. Added met_optimize_alpha_rc() criterion-driven optimisation met_alpha_rc_stream() designs via Random Restart, Simulated Annealing, Genetic Algorithm.

title: OptiSparseMET 0.1.0
text: Added plan_sparse_met_design() providing end--end MET design workflow integrates: Across-environment allocation via allocate_sparse_met(). Per-environment seed feasibility via assign_replication_by_seed(). Environment-specific field design via met_prep_famoptg() met_alpha_rc_stream(), selected design env_design_specs. Mixed design strategies across environments single call. environment’s design engine specified via env_design_specs, named list design = "met_prep_famoptg" design = "met_alpha_rc_stream" selects constructor. Added combine_met_fieldbooks() stack environment-level field books produced met_prep_famoptg() met_alpha_rc_stream() unified MET-level field book standard metadata columns (Environment, LocalDesign, ReplicationMode, SparseMethod, IsCommonTreatment). Handles heterogeneous column sets across environments filling missing columns NA.

title: OptiSparseMET 0.1.0
